settings

pages · 0.4.0 · aj-p-settings

Settings: privacy, what the model can see, and your data, three states of one pushed page (back to You). One render for every platform; desktop puts the masthead in the title block beside the page.

variantplatformmobile · tablet · desktop (default mobile)
variantstateprivacy · visible · data · delete-confirm · devices · only-device · device-signed-out · device-failed · timezone-failed · export-preparing · export-ready · export-empty · export-failed · delete-pending · delete-failed · timezone (default privacy)
variantcontextscreen · walkthrough (default screen)

statedefaultyes: each state as written
statehovern/a: a page; its controls carry their own

stateloadingyes: settings-loading, What it sees with each row's line and value in bones, no row a link yet; "Loading what it can see." announced
stateerroryes: the failed states (device-failed, timezone-failed, export-failed, delete-failed) show their notice
stateemptyyes: export-empty. Every other state has its rows in journal-website.html

Mobile

Privacy: the masthead row inside the page (10-settings-privacy, mobile-web).

You

Privacy

What leaves this deviceEntries, transcripts and moods you allow the model to read are sent only when you use a model feature.
Who processes itAnthropic processes the material needed for answers, notes and reflections.
TrainingYour writing is never used to train anything, at any time.
How long it is keptA deleted item leaves the product at once and stays hidden in storage until you delete your account. Deleting your account removes everything permanently.
Who else can read itNobody. There is no sharing anywhere in this product and no link that works for anyone but you.
Support resourceIf you want to talk to someone, this is always available.Read

What it sees

The model visibility state: two headed lists and a notice (settings-visible).

You

What it sees

It can read

Your entries144 of 148. Four are held out of memory.144
Your recordingsAll 31, as the text they were turned into.31
Your moodsThe five state answer, on the days you gave one.96

It cannot read

Entries you kept out of memoryNever sent, never indexed, never cited. You can see them marked wherever they appear.4
Your audio itselfOnly the text it was turned into. The recordings stay yours.None
Every one of these can be changed, and changing it applies to everything already written, not only to what comes next.
